# orchestra_monitor_order (Resource)

The order monitors are evaluated in. Where two monitors claim the same event, the earlier one wins.

The monitors in `monitor_ids` come first, in that order. Any other monitor follows in the order it already had, so a monitor created outside Terraform does not need listing; a new monitor is placed last. Declare this resource once per workspace. Destroying it leaves the order as it is.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "orchestra_monitor" "muted_sandbox" {
  name     = "Mute sandbox failures"
  match    = { integrations = ["DUCKDB"] }
  group_by = ["pipeline"]
  action   = { mute = true }
}

resource "orchestra_monitor" "warehouse" {
  name     = "Warehouse failures"
  match    = { integrations = ["SNOWFLAKE", "DBT", "DUCKDB"] }
  group_by = ["pipeline"]
}

# The mute rule is evaluated first, so it claims sandbox failures before the
# warehouse monitor can. Monitors not listed here are evaluated after these, in
# the order they already had.
resource "orchestra_monitor_order" "this" {
  monitor_ids = [
    orchestra_monitor.muted_sandbox.id,
    orchestra_monitor.warehouse.id,
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `monitor_ids` (List of String) Monitor IDs to evaluate first, in order. Usually `orchestra_monitor.<name>.id`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always monitor_order: a workspace has one.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A workspace has one monitor order, imported by this fixed ID. The import
# lists every monitor; trim monitor_ids to the ones Terraform should put first.
terraform import orchestra_monitor_order.this monitor_order
```
